metrics.name: First-response SLA attainment
metrics.definition: Tickets with a recorded first response at or below their business-time target divided by all eligible original tickets. The denominator includes recorded responses and unanswered tickets whose deadline passed by quarter-end.
source_refs: tickets.jsonl lines 1–1500 filtered to the eligible first-response cohort

metrics.name: First-response SLA misses
metrics.definition: Among 1,467 eligible tickets, 147 responded above target and 52 remained unanswered past target.
source_refs: tickets.jsonl lines 1–1500 filtered to the eligible first-response cohort

metrics.name: Median time to first resolution
metrics.definition: Median across 1,353 tickets from receipt to first resolved status, excluding customer-wait intervals. Rate components are inapplicable.
source_refs: tickets.jsonl lines 1–1500 with a first $.events[*].status of resolved

metrics.name: Pre-resolution elapsed time in Assigned
metrics.definition: Sum of elapsed hours in Assigned divided by all elapsed hours before first resolution, across tickets with a first resolution.
source_refs: tickets.jsonl lines 1–1500 with a first $.events[*].status of resolved

ambiguity_log.question: Use the first or last recorded resolution?
file_evidence: tickets.jsonl line 15 has a reopened event
ambiguity_log.answer: Measure from receipt to the first resolved event. Subtract intervals beginning in waiting_customer and ending at the next recorded event. The user chose the first resolved event even if the ticket reopened.
The user will discuss next-quarter staffing using the Q2 SLA and delay findings.

file_evidence: tickets.jsonl lines 1–1500 have 1,500 distinct ticket_id values and nested event records
ambiguity_log.answer: Analyze one ticket per JSON line. Keep the event sequence within each ticket.

ambiguity_log.question: What first-response and resolution time targets apply?
file_evidence: tickets.jsonl line 1 has priority and response timestamps
ambiguity_log.answer: User supplied P1/P2/P3/P4 first-response targets of 1/4/8/24 business hours. Count all eligible originals once.

file_evidence: tickets.jsonl lines 1 and 1500 delimit the Q2 KST receipt range
ambiguity_log.answer: Score Q2 2025 KST arrivals at quarter-end. Use weekdays 09:00–18:00 KST, except May 5 and June 6, for the first-response clock. Resolution uses elapsed hours.

ambiguity_log.question: Do tickets marked duplicate_of count separately?
ambiguity_log.answer: User confirmed excluding tickets marked duplicate_of from first-response SLA only. Those IDs link to original tickets in the file.

ambiguity_log.question: Count overdue unanswered tickets as misses or use recorded responses only?
file_evidence: tickets.jsonl line 18 lacks first_response_at and its deadline passed
ambiguity_log.answer: User confirmed counting 54 overdue unanswered tickets before duplicate exclusions. The final eligible cohort contains 52. Exclude the 18 original tickets whose response targets remained open.
The analysis uses one table. No external lookup or event-level join is needed.

file_evidence: tickets.jsonl line 1 has resolved_at and event status without a target field
ambiguity_log.answer: User reported that the resolution SLA targets are unknown.

charts.question: How did first-response attainment change through Q2?
How close were individual responses to their targets?
How widely did customer-wait-adjusted time to first resolution vary?
Which recorded status accounted for the most time before first resolution?

exclusions.reason: 15 tickets linked to originals through duplicate_of. The original tickets are evaluated under the same first-response rules.
18 unanswered original tickets whose first-response deadlines remained open at quarter-end.
52 eligible overdue tickets have no observed first-response duration. They contribute to the compliance denominator as misses.
147 tickets have no first resolved event by quarter-end.
